newsitem.title: UK: Ldn freight - Panamax gains seen checked.
newsitem.headline: Ldn freight - Panamax gains seen checked.

text.p: A surge in dry cargo freight rates in the Panamax category appeared on Wednesday to have been checked, at least for now, shipbrokers said.

Rates are still very firm East of Suez and in the North Atlantic but evidence suggests they may now have started levelling off. The BFI gained a modest 7 points to 1522. Japanese brokers were reported to be forecasting a fall in Pacific rates for Panamaxes but no fixtures have yet been reported to support this view.

Brokers believe that any potential decline will be cushioned by widespread congestion in the world's ports, especially in China. Despite a relative shortage of ironore business Caper activity is said to be increasing and freight levels appear to be appreciating for coal shipments in the Atlantic. Handy-size conditions remain generally dull.

Panamax chartering from US Gulf to the Far East is still the hottest section of the freight market. Continental and Glencore were both believed working tonnage for November shipments to China and there were reports that Dreyfus may have agreed about $26.50 for this business (last fixed $28.00 for mid Nov and $26.50 for end Nov). The US Gulf/Japan trade featured with Mitsubishi's fixture of 52,000 hss on Continental tonnage for Nov 18/28 at $26.25 no combo (last done $26.00 for end Nov) and Oldendorff's fixture of the Marifran-relet Rita d'Amato 69,201 dwt delivery Rotterdam about Nov 25 for a trip via Baltimore with Toepfer's grain stem to Japan at a firm $15,250 daily.

Cargill were reported as saying that a number of Panamaxes were available at $15.00 for their Nov/Dec HSS US Gulf/ Continent. Timios Stavros 64,730 dwt and Meridian Sky 64,293 dwt were rumoured fixed for US Gulf grain business on private terms, and possibly also Captain John L 64,584 dwt for US Gulf/Japan grain on timecharter with Dorval.

The 1981-built Anangel Argonaut 65,668 dwt was reported to be working charterers basis delivery Alexandria out Nov 21 trip via US Gulf to the Far East at $14,250 daily against $13,500 daily. New orders Wednesday included Nidera 50,000 soyabean meal prompt up River and Brazil/China, Cargill for a Panamax delivery Sepetiba Bay early Dec for ironore into the Plate followed by grain to the Continent, and Dreyfus 54,000 HSS PNW/Taiwan for Nov 25/Dec 5. Handy-size grain business was again limited but Lorico fixed Kanaris for 33,000 corn US Gulf to Beirut for Nov 18/25 at a fairly steady $18.00.

Cape America was understood booked by Cetragpa for 110,000 coal Hampton Roads/Ijmuiden for mid Dec at a firmer $6.25 (equivalent to about $6.40 basis Rotterdam) and not on timecharter as originally believed. Other TransAtlantic Caper business included Algarrobo 149,834 dwt rumoured fixed by Rohstoffhandel with ironore to Rotterdam at about $5.50 (loading port disputed) and Cattleya Star 158,570 dwt for direct continuation with Klaveness at the end of a period fixture for a TransAtlantic round, possibly to cover ironore from Boca Grande to Immingham, at a reported $10,000 daily.

Cockerill fixed Rhodos for 110,000 ironore Nouadhibou/Antwerp for Dec 20/30 at $4.75, up about 50 cents from the rate prevailing last week. The Middle East/Indian Ocean continued firm for Panamaxes in the ore and coal trades with charterers conceding 3-5 months period timecharter business in some cases. There were relatively few fresh reports of NoPac or Australian rounds but K Line, having cancelled Achilles 69,000 dwt for an East Australian coal round at $12,200 daily, were understood to have taken Sea Diamond 69,220 dwt instead delivery Mizushima Nov 18/20 at $13,750 daily.

There were occasional reports of fixtures in this category but brokers described demand as patchy or weak. Olympic Melody 29,000 dwt was fixed by Van Ommeren delivery spot Hamburg for 2-4 months redelivery Atlantic at a firm $7,950 daily.
